latest_release.name: v0.45.0
latest_release.body:
### New Features

- Added a **Firefox engine** driven over WebDriver BiDi: pass `--engine firefox` (or set `AGENT_BROWSER_ENGINE=firefox`) with Firefox 150 or newer to drive a local Firefox install with snapshots and `@eN` refs across open and closed shadow roots and iframes, `find` locators, shared form preconditions and error codes (`fill`, `type`, `check`, `uncheck`, `select --by`), right-click, middle-click, and modifier keys (`--button`, `--modifiers`), network routes and HAR capture, `--allowed-domains`, downloads, viewport, media, geolocation, header, and offline emulation, isolated windows, `--pin-tab`, screenshots, PDF export, and dashboard live view (#2205, #2206, #2207, #2208, #2595, #2633)
- Added **Firefox attach mode**: connect to an existing Firefox instance over WebDriver BiDi with `--cdp` or `connect` (including `ws://.../session?devtools=<port>` endpoints), apply live settings in place, and detach on `close` without closing the running browser (#2227)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **keyboard `keydown`, `keyup`, and `press` modifier handling**: `keydown` and `keyup` now send `code`, `keyCode`, `location`, and printable text and carry held modifiers across subsequent keyboard, mouse, and flow-recorder commands. `press` applies US-layout Shift mapping, suppresses printable text for Alt, Control, and Meta chords, and dispatches modifier key events for chords not already held (#2734)
- Fixed **saved flow host rules, write consent, deadlines, and result shaping**: saved host rules now match hostnames regardless of case or a trailing DNS root dot, non-`POST` requests carrying GraphQL queries require write declarations and consent, HTTP preflight cookie and route lookups and in-page fetches stop at the run deadline, empty result lists no longer fail `--fields` or `--where`, and `--limit` shapes only retained rows (#2735)
- Fixed **saved flow replay** finishing before late-reported first-party Chrome requests settle (#2711)
- Fixed **iframe targeting**: `frame` resolves cross-origin, unnamed, and nested iframes by CSS selector or `@ref`, and selector commands, `find` locators, `wait`, `check`, and `uncheck` act inside the selected frame, including same-site cross-origin iframes, without reaching tabs pinned by other sessions (#2737)
- Fixed **`eval` and `console` in iframes**: `eval` runs in the frame selected with `frame` and reports that frame's origin, and `console` and `errors` capture messages from cross-origin iframes on the active tab (#2738)
- Fixed **iframe snapshots and annotated screenshots**: snapshots label iframes by their `title` or `name`, and `screenshot --annotate` places boxes for elements inside iframes in page coordinates, including cross-origin, scrolled, and scaled frames (#2739)
- Fixed **dashboard live view pointer and tabs**: clicks map to the real page size, drags send held buttons, touchpad two-finger taps open the context menu, and a tab that closes itself resyncs the tab bar (#2744)
- Fixed **dashboard live view keyboard and clipboard**: editing shortcuts such as select all, undo, and line navigation reach the page, Option and AltGr characters type, and copy, cut, and paste work through the live view without granting the browser clipboard permissions (#2745)
- Fixed **`state save` collection**: it no longer stalls under `--allowed-domains`, sends requests to previously visited origins, runs their service workers, or brings a temporary tab to the front. It includes origins from attached sessions but not tabs pinned by other sessions, and keeps the previous autosave when collection fails (#2746)
- Fixed **`state list`, `state show`, and bulk storage reads**: `state list` shows modified dates, `state show` reports cookie and origin counts (`cookieCount` and `originCount` in JSON, with `summary` unchanged), and `storage local` and `storage session` keep keys such as `__proto__` (#2747)

### Documentation

- Added the **Firefox engine guide** (`/engines/firefox`) and updated CLI help, MCP tool sche

detail.readme:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured. Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore). See the [Firefox engine guide](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/firefox). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | |---|---|---| | Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) | | Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) | | Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) | | Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) | | Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) | | Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) | | Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) | | Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) | | Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `flow`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) | | Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) | | Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) | Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration). ## Platforms Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host. ## Development Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI pnpm link --global agent-browser install ``` Run the Rust checks from `cli/`: ```bash cargo fmt -- --check cargo clippy cargo test cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process. ## Documentation - [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference - [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration) - [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries - [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0
